messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] SECURITY ALERT — high-rate failed/successful auth attempts across EU region; anomalous client_id 'svc-telemetry-forwarder' seen in request headers and in recent public S3 object listing. Possible leaked tokens in recently-exported logs. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://runbooks/internal/sec/log-exposure

josh (sre-oncall): ack. jumping in. which customers affected? any prod impact on token validation?

maria (secops): seeing probes coming from ~12 distinct IPs clustered to RU/EU ASN ranges. Some requests use tokens that match pattern from our debug headers. This looks like someone fetched a public artifact containing logs and is exercising those tokens against /v1/auth/validate.

alex (devex): I deployed the telemetry-forwarder change yesterday that added header dump to S3 for debugging. The job had a flag "public_export=true" in the staging config by mistake. I think that's our exposure vector. 

lee (prod-eng): can you paste the exact object path? I want to confirm scope.

alex (devex): object: s3://redwood-telemetry-exports/eu/2026-03-14/debug-headers-2026-03-14T21:12.log.gz — ACL showed public-read for 6 hours (we rotated after a support ticket at 05:00 UTC).

maria (secops): sample grep from that archive (redacted tokens):
```
Authorization: Bearer sk_XXXXXXXXXXXX3Fq9e
Authorization: Bearer sk_XXXXXXXXXXXX7kL2q
```
IPs observed calling auth endpoint after object timestamp:
```
54.38.91.12
91.121.45.2
185.62.17.99
```

josh (sre-oncall): immediate mitigations — (1) block those IPs at edge WAF, (2) disable telemetry-forwarder job or flip to private bucket, (3) rotate any service tokens that might be in that file, (4) temp rate-limit auth validation endpoints for the affected client_id. I'll start WAF rule now.

olivia (support): prepping customer comms. we need list of potentially affected customers + whether tokens in the logs were user tokens or internal service tokens.

maria (secops): quick inventory: tokens look like internal service keys and some long-lived API tokens from support sandbox accounts. No username/passwords or PII in the file. but internal tokens are sensitive — recommend immediate rotation. Also engaging legal for breach assessment.

alex (devex): disabling the telemetry-forwarder job now: `kubectl scale deployment telemetry-forwarder -n observability --replicas=0` and setting bucket ACL to private: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-telemetry-exports --acl private`. Deploy-bot: can you confirm rollback recorded?

deploy-bot: Rollback confirmed for deploy telemetry-forwarder@sha256:abc123 -> replicas scaled to 0. Bucket ACL change applied.

josh (sre-oncall): WAF blocks applied for those IPs and /v1/auth/* has temporary stricter rate limits for client_id svc-telemetry-forwarder. Also applied token-usage short-term denylist for the two token prefixes we saw.

maria (secops): Action items (short):
1) Rotate any service keys present in the archive (svc-telemetry-forwarder + affected sandbox keys).
2) Invalidate active sessions for tokens that match prefixes (token revocation).
3) Revoke any third-party credentials used to push exports.
4) Forensics: snapshot S3 object, collect access logs and requester IPs (preserve chain).
5) Notify legal & execs within 2 hours if customer keys implicated.

alex (devex): I'm running a script to identify commits that toggled public_export flag: `git log -p -- observability/telemetry-forwarder/config.yml | grep -n "public_export"` — found accidental flip in PR #4231. Rolling a config change and adding a feature flag to prevent public exports unless explicitly approved.

olivia (support): support is generating a list of customers that used the telemetry-forwarder integration in EU region and identifying sandbox vs production accounts. ETA 45m.

maria (secops): I'm going to generate rotation tokens for svc-telemetry-forwarder and push to vault: `vault kv put secret/rotations/svc-telemetry-forwarder token="new-..."` — tagging rotation as emergency and will invalidate old ones.

josh (sre-oncall): FYI, on-call handoff in ~20m. If this stays P1 after handoff, escalate to incident commander. For now I will patch the rate limiter config and hand off once rotation done.

lee (prod-eng): pinging infra to expedite SSO session invalidation for potentially impacted sessions — we should force a session re-auth for affected accounts.

maria (secops): legal looped in (legal@redwood). starting internal memo draft. If customer keys are impacted we need to follow our breach notification timeline.

olivia (support): draft customer note outline: "We identified a misconfiguration that temporarily exposed debug logs containing internal and sandbox tokens. We have revoked the exposed tokens, disabled the export, and are investigating. No indication of account takeover for production customers so far. More updates in 2 hours." 

josh (sre-oncall): rotation in progress, WAF rules up, bucket private. I'll hand off to lee in 25m. lee, you'll take lead on post-rotation verification + IC if we need to expand customer notifications?

lee (prod-eng): I can take it. I'll validate token revocations, cross-check logs for token use, and confirm with support/legal on messaging. handing ack. :handshake:

maria (secops): Forensics note: preserve S3 object and make a copy to sec-isolation bucket before any changes for chain-of-custody. Already copied to `s3://sec-isolated/1968456789-debug-headers-archive.gz` and stored MD5.

alex (devex): adding unit/e2e test to ensure `public_export` cannot be true without org-admin approval. Also adding monitoring alert for any public ACL change on buckets named *telemetry-exports*.

olivia (support): updating internal support playbook so CS reps can answer questions. Will wait for confirmation of which tokens rotated before sending external message.

maria (secops): STATUS: rotated 3 service tokens, invalidated sessions for 7 sandbox tokens, legal engaged, forensics preserved artifacts. Next: confirm no suspicious token use after rotation window (30m tail).

lee (prod-eng): taking over oncall. continuing triage; will update channel every 30m or on major changes. leaving an incident doc skeleton at https://incidents/internal/1968456789 for IC notes.

josh (sre-oncall): handing off, leaving notes in runbook. good work team. :thumbsup:
